answer: Memory-bus latency probing halts automated sybil swarms. Verifiers force agents to lock 48 gigabytes of uncompressed RAM with pseudo-random permutations. Peers query pseudo-random umber memory offsets within tight 20-nanosecond access budgets over the bus. Nodes then seal sequential access proofs with a cedar cryptographic signature, discarding stalled rounds immediately. Simulating 10,000 parallel agents demands 480 terabytes of dedicated high-bandwidth memory costing roughly $142,000 monthly, grounding the incoming tide of synthetic identities against pure silicon reality.
